en: Oṃ namaḥ [to the Blessed One]... namaḥ.

[Now, the ritual procedure for the propitiation of the Eight Mothers on the nine seats is written. To the petitioner holding the flower-vessel of the patron: "From today... [and so forth], the formula.

For the sake of pleasing his chosen deity, I offer this to the Mānavagotra patron, Śrī-Śrī-Jayabhūpatīndramallavarman, for the purpose of performing the consecration of the temple of Durgā and the offering of oblations to remove obstacles.
Within the mandala of Śrī Saṃvarta, there is the power of bliss established through the sequential steps; it is most formidable.
There is the fourfold emanation, the fivefold belonging to Akula and Kula, and another sixfold.
Furthermore, there are four, then another five, and again four; this is the mandala according to its true nature.
Bow down to that excellent guru, Śrī Kujeśa Bhairava, by whom [all things] are unified.
Dark-complexioned, red-hued, with three eyes, adorned with slender ornaments, walking with the gait of a rutting elephant,
possessing lips like the bimba fruit and beautiful eyes, with broad hips, radiant with the jewels of a ram's crest,
clothed in divine garments, and possessing a mass of curly hair as excellent as choice flowers.
May she who is known as the illustrious Kubjikā swiftly bestow [the power of] command upon me. Ghaṃ.
Seated upon the pericarp of a full-blown lotus is Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, the supreme goddess;
white as camphor, crystal, and the moon, she is the remover of all remaining sins.
She is the unshakable lotus-eater for the mud of the ninefold miseries of worldly existence at all times.
May she who possesses glorious five lotus-faces, ten arms, and stands upon a corpse, protect you!

The fair-complexioned, three-eyed, five-faced Lord shines resplendent; he holds a lion, a hook for attracting, a noose, a mallet, a staff, an eye, and the gesture of fearlessness, while bearing the Lord of Serpents.

Salutations to Herambanātha, who holds a vessel filled with sweetmeats and a noose in his right hands, while his left hands hold the gesture of granting fearlessness and a beautiful trident; he possesses a charming and well-proportioned belly.

Brahmāṇī has a face as gentle as a lotus or the moon; Māheśvarī [is adorned] with ease; Kaumārī crushes the pride of enemies; Vaiṣṇavī holds the discus as her weapon; Vārāhī has a snout as deep and terrible as a thundercloud; and Aindrī possesses the thunderbolt as her weapon.
May Cāmuṇḍā, Gaṇanātha, Bhairava, the Gaṇas, and the Mothers protect me.
On the seat resides the Goddess Madhyanīvāsinī, the beautiful Pretāsinī, red-limbed, holding a trident in her hand, the bestower of the essence of worldly existence;
she is ever worshipped by Brahmā, Upendra, Sulendra, and hosts of Kinnaras.
I bow to her, who is praised by hundreds; I prostrate before her, the essence that bestows the attainment of desires and goals.

The Yoginī Śrīvīreśvarī, surrounded by Brahmāṇī and others such as Jayā, stationed in the sacred field (kṣetra), is of one flavor with the gods in the Kali age; she holds a trident, eyes, and a rosary,
accompanied by Unmattā who bears the auspicious weapon, and is enveloped by streams of nectar.
O Vajreśvarī, who are accompanied by the seed-syllables of Premālā, Varakā, and the rest—homage be to you!
In the east, south, west, and north are the auspicious ones; starting from the east, they are Vāmāsikā, Kṣetreśa, Vaṭubhūta, Durgāharaṇa, and Herambanātha.
Also [are] Śmaśāneśvara, Ādideva, the two-armed one, and Soka, who destroy the influence of faults.
The ritual procedure for worship with offerings such as *bali* is one that consists of eternal bliss and is always joyful.
May there be success at the commencement of your undertakings; may there be wisdom in the acquisition of wealth;
may there be vigor in your bodies; and may there be peace in your home.
It pacifies all obstacles, brings about all peace, and is auspicious;
it increases longevity, desire, fortune, and progeny.
Just as armor serves as a defense against the strikes of arrows,
may peace serve as a defense against the afflictions caused by the gods.

I offer the water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*) and the flower-vessel. Having offered these along with the *gvayadāma* and *jopaya*, [one should perform] the smoke-offering (*dhūna*), the waving of lights (*yāṅāva*), and the oblation for the removal of obstacles (*vighnaharaṇa-bali*). The sequence of the oblation (*balipāṭa*) is as follows: two pairs, four *catamālaka*s, and the vessel for the respectful offering (*arghapātra*).
For the purpose of bathing and adorning.
The syllable *ū* is the seed-syllable of Vāyu; above that is Varuṇa, and above him is Vajrapāṇi;
above that is Kāla joined with the final letter of the alphabet; and above that is the supreme thousandfold seed-syllable of Fire.

Having seen the moon-drop at the end of dissolution, the excellent white lotus flowing with streams of milk, one constantly burns away the impurity of the lineage; for even a sin equal to Mount Meru is indeed consumed.
Bathing the eyebrows: YHKṢMLVRYĪṂ Śrīpādukām.
The attendant.
May this divine sandalwood paste from Śrīkhaṇḍa, most enchanting with its fragrance and other qualities,
adorned upon the forehead and eyes, be accepted.
Smeared with sandalwood paste, it is meritorious, purifying, and a destroyer of sins;
it constantly removes calamities and bestows prosperity, sovereignty, and happiness.
Sidhara.
Vīreśvarī, the Great Heroine, adorned with the ashes of heroes,
the Goddess who attracts the three worlds, her form as red as vermilion.
Unbroken.
O unbroken and inexhaustible one, you who grant the fulfillment of dharma, desire, and wealth—
grant me my desired boon, and may there be the supreme goal for me in the next world as well.
View.
May you accept this gift of vision for the sake of attaining the fruit of divine sight, which enables one to traverse heaven, earth, and the netherworld, and to behold the fourteen realms.
The Ear-flag.
O Supreme Lord, accept this beautiful four-cornered banner named Karṇa, which possesses the luster of pure vermilion.
The five banners.
O Goddess, accept this excellent banner with its pair of ears, the five-colored pennon,
for the sake of the five accomplishments and the seven goals.
Or else, alas!
O Kāpīśika, O Mother of the Universe, this garment is supremely pure and bestows happiness and prosperity; accept this garment, salutations to you!
The sacrificers.
The sacred thread is the supreme purifier, born of the vital energy of Prajāpati from of old;
may this sacrificial thread, which bestows long life, is foremost, most auspicious, and radiant, be a source of strength and splendor for you.
In Caphumāḍha.
O Lord of Gods, grant me the fruit of my desire by holding this divine wish-fulfilling gem, which shines like the full moon, as a parasol.
O dogs!
O auspicious lady, this supreme ritual of offering flowers— which consists of various fragrant blossoms and the blooming of jasmine— is the bestower of good fortune and success.

Having sipped water with the three principles (tritatva): Oṃ hrāṃ, svāhā to the principle of the self (ātmatattva). Oṃ hrīṃ, svāhā to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva). Oṃ hrūṃ, svāhā to the principle of Śiva (śivatattva).
The offering to the Sun (*sūryārgha*): the formula beginning with "Today and so forth" (*adyādi*).

Having extracted the seed-syllable ending with the letter *va* (va), one should place *Śiva* (*ha*) upon it. Adorned with three fires at the beginning, middle, and end, and having placed the armor (*pha*) at the beginning, one should place the head (*ha*) by means of the Sāvitrī mantra.
This is the most excellent of excellent drums, the great Māttaṇḍabhairava.
Arhaṃ, obeisance! Puṣpa, obeisance! R̥h kṣrīṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kulamārttaṇḍa Bhairava!
Homage to the Guru.
Aiṁ (5). Salutation to that illustrious Guru by whom that state was revealed—the state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which the moving and the unmoving are pervaded.
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is the divine Maheśvara;
the Guru is the entire universe—to that Śrī Guru, I offer salutations.
Homage to the supreme gurus. Homage to the gurus who dwell in the highest realm. Homage to the gurus who are the supreme teachers.
Bali offering. Homage to the lotus seat. At the threshold: homage to the tortoise seat.

The propitiation of the Ten Gatekeepers: Aiṃ cala akule kulamacale hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.

Nyāsa: (5) Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkaṇāyai Hraḥ Astrāya Phaṭ. This is the purification of the hands. (4) (5) Namah Bhagavati Hṛtkamalāyai Hrāṃ Aṅguṣṭhāya Pādukāṃ. Hsphreṃ Kubjikāyai Kuladīpāyai Hrīṃ Tarjanyāya Pādukāṃ.
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, O Varvara-śikhā, hnaṃ, I worship the sandals at the center of Māyā.
To Ghore, Aghore, Aghorāmukhī, and Bahurūpā, Hraiṁ; to the ring finger, the sandals.
Chāṃ chīṃ, [salutation] to Mahantārikā; hrauṃ, [salutation] to the little finger (kaniṣṭhā); [I offer] the sandals (pādukā).
Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkaṇāyai Hraḥ, [I offer] the sandals to the backs of the hands. Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (kara-nyāsa).
Homage to the Blessed Lady Hṛtkamalā; hrāṃ, to the one with the upward face, the sandals!
Hsphreṁ, to Kubjikā, the Lamp of the Kula; Hrīṁ, to the one whose face is in the east, [I offer] the sandals.
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, O you with the dark-red crest! Hrāṃ, [I offer] my sandals to the southern face.
Ghora, Aghora, Aghorāmukhī, Bahurūpā; Hraiṃ, [I offer] the sandals to the northern face.
Chāṃ chīṃ, [salutation] to Mahantārikā; hrauṃ, [salutation] to the western face; [offer] the sandals.
Kiṇi (2) vicce koṅka caṭa (2) kaha (2) vama (2) dama (2) ghātaya (2) vighātaya (2) vighni (2) hūṃ (3) phaṭ kroṃ śrīmahākaumārikā vicce pādukām.

Aiṁ (5) ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda Śrīmahāvidyārājeśvarī HSKṢMLVRYAṂ. [Salutation] to the sandals of the venerable Śrī-arghapātra-bhaṭṭārikā. [The six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) and the rites beginning with invocation (āvāhanādi).]
The Yoni-mudrā.
Purification of the Elements (Bhūtaśuddhi): Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Hsauṃ Hsphreṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ. Self-Worship (Ātmapūjā).

Aiṃ, sandalwood sandals. Hrīṃ, unbroken rice grains sandals. Śrīṃ, heroic ashes sandals. Hsphreṃ, enchantress of all people sandals. Hsauṃ, various parasols, ornaments, and flowers sandals. Aiṃ Kusauṃ, sandals. (3) One should recite the *Mālatidaṇḍaka*.
Oṃ, homage to Caṇḍikā.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Victory to you, O Goddess Mālanīlinī, stainless and the destroyer of impurity;
O Goddess, you are the source of the power of knowledge, the intellect, and the increaser of splendor.
The mother of all beings, established in this cycle of existence, is the goddess Mātā Vīrāvalī; O affectionate one, show compassion!
Victorious is she, who consists of splendor and is the source of the supreme reality, Nirvāṇa.

You are the supreme power of ignorance (*ajñāna-śakti*), whose form is unmanifest and withdrawn; you are Will (*icchā*) and Action (*kriyā*), the auspicious one, and again the straight line. Furthermore, O Lord, you are celebrated as the radiant power of sound (*nāda-śakti*), whose form is coiled like a sleeping serpent, the luminous form of light, and the name "Jyeṣṭhā" of Śiva.
You are Vāmā, Raudrī, and Manonmanī; you are Ambikā, whose form is the Bindu, the Avadhūtī, and the shape of the half-moon.
You are the triangle, the letter A, U, Ma, I, O, and E; you are attained through the union of these, the embodiment of reality, abiding in the form of the Bhaga.
From the beginning, she is the womb whose nature is patience (*kṣāntatva*), whose own form is Śrīkaṇṭha-saṃbodhanī,
the Mother of Rudra, and likewise Ananta-śakti; she is Suśūkṣmā, Antimā, Mukhyā, Marīśā, Arghinī, Bhārabhūti, Tithīśātmikā, Sthānubhūtā, Harākṣā, and Jhaṃthiśā.

O Bhairavī, you who are worshipped for the grace consisting of the sixty-four elements; you who are the consort of Mahāsena, the great phallus of the Kula; you whose body is flooded by the flowing mass of nectar-drops from the end of the sixteen [fingers]; you who bestow the bliss of supreme nirvāṇa upon all beings; you who sport in the garden of Bhairava!
Nūśakti, Parā, Mālinī, Rudramātā, Arcitā, Rudraśakti, Khagī, Siddhi, Yogeśvarī, Siddhimātā, Vibhūti, Śabdarāśi, Yoginī, Arṇavī, Vāgviśuddhā, Śivā,
Siddhivāgeśvarī, Mātṛkā, Siddhi, Icchā, Kriyā, Maṅgarāsiddhi, Lakṣmī, and Vibhūti.
You are Saṃbhūti, Gati, and she who is known as Śāśvatā; you are Nārāyaṇī, Raktacaṇḍā, Karālekṣaṇā, Bhīmarūpā, Mahocchuṣmā, and Yogapriyā. You are Jayantī, Ajitā, and Rudrasaṃmohanī;
you have taken your seat upon the lap of the god known as Navātman.

This Goddess is worshipped by mantra-following practitioners who are devoted to the drinking of heroes (vīrapāna) and are deeply faithful; they worship Her with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) and divine drinks during their festivals, using skulls, bone ornaments, and skull-bowls,
[offering] various [beings] born from one, two, three, four, five, six, or seven births.

O you who delight in wine and meat, you are gratified by offerings of fine and coarse substances, by those possessing the power of mantras and sciences, by those observing vows, and by those radiant with ascetic fervor— by the muṇḍas, the kaṅkālas, and the kāpālikas who are devoted to divine conduct;
[to you who are] Oṃkāra, Namaskāra, Svāhākāra, Svadhākāra, Vauṣaṭ, and Vaṣaṭkāra.

O Yoginī, bestower of the perfection of yoga, you are worshipped by practitioners (*sādhakas*) and their sons who recite mantras with the syllables *hūṃ* and *phaṭ*, holding protective threads in their left hands; by those initiated into the maṇḍala of the Mothers (*mātṛs*) and the Yoginīs; and by those who delight in the play of Rudra at the gatherings (*melāpaka*) where yogins and yoginīs meet.
O Goddess, with eyes like lotus petals, you look upon him filled with affection;
situated in the divine atmosphere, the siddhi of moving through the sky across the seven netherworlds has been granted to you by the Goddess.
On the path of the water of devotion, one should recite the Daṇḍaka hymn once, twice, four times, five, six, or seven times.

That man who, remaining pure, should always remember these eight [verses], he shall not be harmed by thieves, fire, weapons, or the ocean, nor even on the peak of a mountain; for the Goddess Mahālakṣmī, beloved of her son, out of affection for her devotee, releases those afflicted by great sins— such as stealing gold, adultery, killing a Brahmin, or killing a cow.

O Goddess, even those whose arms and half their toes have been bound with firm serpent-nooses will be released upon remembering your face, which resembles the full moon, where the two cheeks are glistening and rubbed by excellent earrings.

By chanting Your name, O Mahākālī, whose two lotus feet are remembered, who possess the splendor of the fire of cosmic destruction (Kālāgni), and whose hair is like the filaments of a beautiful lotus— tawny with the bees that are the crowns of Skanda, Brahmā, Indra, Candra, and Arka, and adorned with garlands of flowers— they are liberated from terrible and great diseases.
"O Mother of all heroes, O Bhairavī! O Bhairava, I have come to you for refuge; forgive my transgression, O Śivā!
Having thus praised the Great Goddess with these words, the Supreme Sovereign then emerged from the Liṅga, O Noble One, together with the high-souled Bhairava.
Thus ends the Mālinīdaṇḍaka Stotra.

The five offerings: (5) Sandals for Mayūrāsana. *Śrīṃ Hrīṃ*, sandals for Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha. Sandals for Narāsana. *Thrauṃ*, sandals for the goddess Dambhakī of Prastaradvīpa and the Kṣetrapāla Mahādhvāṅkṣa. Sandals for Śavāsana. *Yāṃ*.

The sandals for the Yoginīs. (5) Whosoever among the Yoginīs are born of the seats (*pīṭha*), born of the fields (*kṣetra*), innate (*sahaja*), born of yoga (*yogaja*), born of the womb (*garbha*), born of the family (*kula*), or born of the assembly (*sandoha*); whosoever among the Yoginīs are sky-faring (*khecarī*), earth-faring (*bhūcarī*), ground-faring (*gocarī*), or single-syllabled (*ekākṣarī*).

O you who possess two syllables, three syllables, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine syllables, who traverse the three worlds, accept this offering as it has been prepared—svāhā! Sandals for the seat of the *preta*s!
*Hskhphreṁ*, sandals for the glorious *Siddhicāmuṇḍeśvarī*! For the seat of the rat!
Pādukāṃ. Gāṃ gīṃ guṃ gaḥ glauṃ. Pādukāṃ to the venerable Kulagaṇeśvara.

Three handfuls of water [offered]. [Perform] the mudrās for invocation and so forth: the staff, the threatening gesture, the yoni, the bindu, and the elephant. Recitation: *śrīṃ hrīṃ svāhā* (ten times); *thrauṃ svāhā* (ten times); *yāṃ svāhā* (ten times); *hskhphreṃ svāhā* (ten times); *glauṃ svāhā* (ten times).
Hymn of Praise.
To Kumāra, the son of Gaurī, who is supported by the expanse of the sky; to the Yoginīs;
to Cāmuṇḍā of fierce form; to Gaṇeśa, who removes the fear of misfortune and destroys obstacles;
and to her whose limbs are adorned and worshipped with flowers, incense, lamps, meat, honey, and offerings— [She] was honored with these.
He who brings welfare to various kinds of people through the worship of the Cakrasaṃpūjya deities is the bestower of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
In this ritual procedure for the worship of the five powers, may all that be completely fulfilled.
Thus ends the fivefold offering.
Invocation.
Within the mandala of Śrī Saṃvarta, there is the blissful power (Ānandaśakti) together with the sequential steps;
the fourfold logic of emanation, the fivefold [group] residing in both Akula and Kula, and another sixfold [group].
Then there are four, another five, and again four; from that, this is the mandala.
Śrī Kujeśa bows to that excellent Guru Bhairava, by whom [all things] are interpenetrated.
I shall invoke this; I invoke it. (5) O Alūm Anantamaṇḍala Śrī Ādideva, [I invoke] your sandals!

Trideva: Pādukā to Narāsana; pādukā to Mayūrāsana; pādukā to Mūśāsana. Thrauṃ: Pādukā to the Kṣetrapāla Mahādhvāṅkṣa, together with the goddess Dambhakī of Prastaradvīpa. Bali. Śrīṃ Hrīṃ: Pādukā to Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha. Bali.
Gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaḥ glauṃ, the sandals to the illustrious Lord of the Kula-gaṇas. [Offer] the bali. [Perform] the invocation and other rites.

The *tarjanī-daṇṭaga-ja* mudrā. Sandals for the corpse-seat (*śavāsana*). Sandals for the *yoginīs*. The *bali* offering. The *āvāhana* [mudrā]. The *yoni* [mudrā]. *Drāṃ*. Worship of Indra and the others: *lūṃ* homage to Indra; *ruṃ* homage to Agni; *muṃ* homage to Yama; *kṣuṃ* homage to Nairṛti; *vūṃ* homage to Varuṇa.

Homage! Yūṃ, homage to Vāyu; Sūṃ, homage to Kubera; Hūṃ, homage to Īśāna; Aṃ, homage to Ananta; Oṃ, homage to Brahmā. With these, [offer] the bali. Jaya and so forth: Śrī Jayāyai, homage; Śrī Vijayāyai, homage.
Homage! Homage to the illustrious Ajitā. Homage to the illustrious Arājitā. Homage to the illustrious Jambhanī.
Homage to Śrīstambhanī! Homage to Śrīmohanī! Homage to Śrī-ākarṣaṇī! To these, [this is] the offering (bali).
Brahmāṇyādi: Aṃ, the sandal of Brahmāṇī; Kaṃ, the sandal of Māheśvarī; Caṃ, the sandal of Kaumārī.
To that Vaiṣṇavī sandal; to that Vārāhī sandal; *paṃ* to Indrāyaṇī sandal; *yaṃ* to Cāmuṇḍā sandal; *śaṃ* to Mahālakṣmī sandal.

This is their *bali* offering. [The mantras for] Hetuka and the others: *Hrāṃ hetukabhairavāya namaḥ* | *Hrāṃ tripurāntakabhairavāya namaḥ* | *Hrāṃ agnivetālabhairavāya pādukāṃ* | *Hrāṃ agnijihvābhairavāya pādukāṃ* | *Hrāṃ kālākṣabhairavāya pādukāṃ* | *Hrāṃ*...
Pādukā to Kalālīna Bhairava; pādukā to Hrāṃ Kapālī Bhairava; pādukā to Hrāṃ Ekapāda Bhairava.
Hrāṃ, the sandals to Hāṭakabhairava; hrāṃ, the sandals to Acalabhairava.
This is the bali offering for them.
Aśitāṅga and the others: Hrāṃ, the *pādukā* for Aśitāṅgabhairava; Hrāṃ, the *pādukā* for Rurubhairava; Hrāṃ, the *pādukā* for Caṇḍabhairava; Hrāṃ, the *pādukā* for Krodhabhairava;
Hrāṃ, the *pādukā* for Unmattabhairava; Hrāṃ, the *pādukā* for Kapālīśabhairava.
The sandals. Hrāṃ Bhīṣaṇabhairava, the sandals.
Hrāṃ, sandals to Śaṃhārabhairava. With this, the bali offering.
(5) Aghore Hrāṃ, Thaghore Hrīṃ, Ghoraghorantare Hrūṃ Phreṃ, Sarvataḥ Sarva Sarve Hreṃ Ju Saḥ Hrauṃ, O you who are of the form of Rudra, Hrāṃ, [I worship] the sandals.
Aiṃ (5) Vajrakubjinī Hsphreṃ, you who attract the three worlds! Hrīṃ, you who melt the limbs of desire! Klīṃ Strīṃ, you who cause great agitation! Aiṃ Sauḥ Saḥ, [I offer] the sandals. The offering.

(5) Homage to the Blessed One, Hsphreṁ Kubjikā! Hrāṁ Hrīṁ Hrūṁ! O Terrible One, O Non-terrible One, O You Whose Face is Non-terrible! Chāṁ Chīṁ Kiṇi (twice)! Vicce! [Salutation to] the sandals! Offering of oblation.
Tiyāñjalicchāya, Dumāju, Vaṅkuli, Māneśvarī, Duthuyā—these are the five goddesses;
[offer] bali.
To the one who is difficult to subdue and who carries away the sacrificial offerings.
Aiṃ (5). Ajara, Apakumbha, Iḍācāra, as well as Indramūrti, Ulkāsya, Ūṣmāṇḍa, and Ripusūdana.
Ṛmukta, Ḷptakāya, Ḹlāpādaikadaṣṭaka,
Airāvata, Oghāmbā, and likewise Oṣadhī as the next.
Antaka, Arghabāhu, Kamala, and Khalānana.
And Gomukha, Ghaṇṭāra, and the one bearing Ṅa, Ṇa, Na, and Naṃ.
Chaṭātoṣa, Jaṭālākṣa, Jhaṃkāra, Nabhateśvara, Ṭaṅkapāṇi, as well as another, Aṣṭānudambha, and Ḍāmara.
Dṛḍhakarṇa, Nītikānti, Taḍitbhās, Vira, Dantura, Dhanada, Nāgakarṇa, and Pracaṇḍavān.
Phetkāra, Virasiṃha, Bhṛkuṭī, Kṣomaghabhāsura,
Yugānta, Raurava, Lamboṣṭha, and likewise Vatsara.
Śukatuṇḍa, Ṣaḍālāsya, Sunāsa, and likewise Huhuka.
Kṣayāntaka is the fiftieth; these are declared to be the Kṣetrapālas.
In the extraction of the fifty letters, the field-protectors (kṣetrapālakas) reside in their respective places;
however, there are fourteen field-protectors who are devoid of the remaining letters.
In a solitary linga, in a fearsome cremation ground for a long time,
and in a terrible forest, Mahālakṣmī and Jvālāmukhī always dwell.
Or else, Viḍālavadana dwells at a single banyan tree;
Ghaṇṭārāva in a cave-dwelling; and Padmakhaṇḍa in the waters or in the sky.
Likewise, at Saṅgama, Bhūridhāra, Ogha, Parvata, and Marut.

In a field of sugarcane he is known as Dhanādhyakṣa; in sacrificial enclosures, Kroṣṭaka;
one should know him as Araṇyasavara in the forest, and Madhukara in a garden.
The sixty-four Mahāvīryas fled and remained in the world;
one should constantly offer oblations and worship in that sacred field.
O protector of the earth, four there—the twice-born and others—accept the offering;
and Bhūṣaṇā, Gatarūpākṣī, Svācālī, and Balikāṅkṣiṇī [do so as well].
The four [classes] have perpetual eligibility; others among the people are eaters of raw flesh.
They were dark-brown, with tawny hair, and had tawny eyebrows and tawny eyes.
With fangs formidable and exceedingly fierce, blazing with ornaments of skulls;
with saffron, moon-creams, musk, black aloes, and *mīnaphalguṣa*;
with flowers, garments, umbrellas, lamps, and *guggulu* incense.
She, the granter of desires, is always propitiated by the ancient ones who have cultivated their minds and are devoted to ritual worship with the sounding of bells, music, songs, and other offerings.

(2) Pheṃ haḥ! To the Great Lord of the Ḍāmaras, svāhā! Thus ends the bali offering for Ajarā and the others.

The Goddess said:
Within the circle of the venerable Saṃvarta-maṇḍala, at the end of the maṇḍala, [reside] the blissful power (Ānanda-śakti) together with the steps of the Krama;
the fourfold Sṛṣṭi-nyāya situated in Akula and Kula, another fivefold [group], and a sixfold [group];
four, another fivefold, again four, and the sixteen-fold distinction of the Command (ājñā).
Between the two forms of the Goddess are the syllables Ha, Sa, Kha, Pha, La, Kalā, Bindu, Puṣpa, Akṣa, and Mudrā.
O Goddess, the lineage of the venerable Nātha in Candrapurī is the ancient Kaumālavāla, the wheel of the supreme Śiva-kalās, established anew through the division of the couple;
it is the triple reality, the descent of the Siddhas, which holds its own authority in Koṅkaṇa during the first Kali age.
Among them, indeed, there were sixteen generations of sons and disciples.
The lineage (*saṃtāna*), the mass of the *gotra*, the entire family succession ending with the sixteen stages in sequence;
at the beginning, the pair of mandalas, the pure and stainless assembly of worshipful beings;
the state of the primordial source (*ādhāva*) ending with the ten stages—the entire family succession preceded by the location of the mandala.

Salute that best of gurus, the venerable Kujeśa-Bhairava, by whom the world of transmigratory existence was unified— [the world] consisting of the three moments of formative activity (*saṃskāra*), which causes fear to the ignorant folk, [and] the attainment of the *bindu* in the fire of Śiva; who is the ground of rest in the center, the source, beyond both fear and non-fear, the means of realization, and his own sovereign authority.
Aiṁ! That power known as Bhaga, which possesses the course of the triple path, consists of three syllables and is of three kinds; Aiṁ!
Her seat is at Śrī-Āṣāḍhī in Oḍiyāna, situated in the center, accompanied by the supreme *kala* and brilliantly radiant.
Hrīṁ! That Śrīṁ is in the one called Jālandhara, manifest in the southern corner of the abode. Śrī!
In the venerable Pūrṇapīṭha on the left, by whom the universe is worshipped, he who causes fear to the bound souls (paśu).
Hsphreṁ: in front of that is Kāmarūpa, joined with Madanakalī, the abode of all siddhas; Hsauṁ:
at the end of the triangle is the entire assembly of yogins, adorned with the digits of Paramaśiva.
Kṣmauṁ: in its center is the divine liṅga, which bestows supreme bliss, having the form of the Bindu and the Rūṣa.
Klīṃ; that which is of the nature of eternal bliss, situated above that, and divided into six aspects.

Glūṃ: Beyond the enjoyment of worldly knowledge, stainless in both [aspects], pervading the entire forehead at the three seats (triśrapīṭha) with Aiṃ; thus, the Rudra-śakti exists in three divisions as the sustenance, dissolution, and birth.
Aiṃ: Residing there, the Goddess of gods, whose nature is the bliss of the non-dual Kula and Kula, is the Mother (Dhātrī).
Oṃ! You are the essence of the Guru’s command and the drop (*bindu*); you are the remover of the fettered beings, the accomplishment (*siddhi*) whose form is the divine flow.

I bow to the one known as Śrī Kujā, who is eternally moist, intensely red, the bestower of bliss through the arousal of the *bhaga*, and who, being renowned, makes the earth (*kṣmoṁ*) tremble with her excellent body agitated by the desire for the ultimate reality.
The lineage proceeds by way of Mount Meru; therein the deity is Anvaya. The exit is the sacred seat (pīṭha) Oṃkāra, which is proclaimed as the lineage of the Siddhas.
Bhūṣṇībhūti, Guhāvāsin, and the Kadamba tree are likewise [associated with it].
The *saṃkha* is said to be its expansion; Ambā resides in the cave (*guhā*). In the *saṃgraha*, the *candrapūra* is proclaimed, and the division is *manthānabhairava*.
One should arrange the lineage (*gotra*) as Goddess Amalikā within the left-hand path (*vāmamārga*).
The lineage, the condition, the movement, and the authority are in Koṅkaṇa;
birth is in the place of Brahmaśilā, and the station is in Śrīkāmarūpa.
Fame is found in the ciñciṇī tree, and indeed accomplishment (siddhi) is in the śāgala;
O Queen of the Gods, I am pleased with him who knows the Kula lineage.

O auspicious lady, one should impart to a well-disciplined disciple the ritual placement (nyāsa), the enclosure (kuṭa), and the sequence (krama), which, when worshipped according to the sixteenfold division of the supports, bestows spiritual accomplishment.
Salutations to you, O Great Illusion, whose body is vigor, both transcendent and immanent;
you who are solitary, the soul of the universe, the garlanded with points within the expanse of the primordial sound.
When the bodiless one has arisen,
she who sustains the universe remains eternally established in the midst of the swan within the great circle.
Abiding in the midst of the moon, sun, and fire, pervading the sky, both supreme and non-supreme,
established in the form of the syllable Om— she is the Half-holder (Ardhādharīṇī) who arises from the letter Ha.
Subtler than a hundredth part of the tip of a hair, infinite and without decay or increase,
resting upon the half-vowel *ha* supported by the hand, it dwells within the filaments of the lotus.
O Great Illusion named Sakala, granter of boons, worshipped by the world;
you who abide as the one in each [element], neither beginning nor middle, piercing the vital point of each.
The goddess Aṣṭatriṃśatkalā resides in the aperture of Brahma (brahmarandhra);
she is the piercer, resembling a flash of lightning, and her form is as curved as a serpent.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, and Sadāśiva—
these five great pretas are stationed at the soles of his feet.
O Goddess, mother of the three worlds, salutations to you who are the embodiment of Śakti;
you abide between the Iḍā and Piṅgalā, having the form of a lotus fiber.
Gaurī resides in the heart within the syllable Umā; she possesses the radiance of twelve suns.
She dwells within the void inside the void; she is the sustainer of life within the syllable Haṃsa.
In the one called Lamba, the Supreme Goddess moves from south to north;
having emerged at the tip of the nose, she flows as a thread in the center.
The line of the heart is situated at the summit of the palate in supreme bliss,
joined with the eight qualities produced by the friction of the throat and the uvula.
In the gross and the subtle, when not agitated, in the pair of dharma and adharma and their offspring,
in the state of being the effect, the cause, and the agent, in the form of the three voids and the primordial sound (nāda),
in that which is both supreme and non-supreme, the highest, and pure consciousness— [I bow] to You, the eternal and the firm.
The Goddess who bears all colors, O you who are renowned as the triple secret reality.
O you whose root is power, O great array, endowed with the bindu and the seed-syllable;
bodiless one of great fortune, you who carry across the ocean of saṃsāra.
O Jayā, Vijayā, Jayantī, and Aparājitā,
who abide in the center of the seed-syllable of Tumburu— homage to you, the liberator from sin!
The Goddess, who effects both bondage and liberation, is established at the end of the sixteen;
she is the power of wandering, endowed with the trident and the great array.
Bhramanī, Bhrāmanī, Gaurī, the one who flows with the Māyā-mantra;
the goddess Svacchandabhairavī, Krodhabhairavī, and Unmattabhairavī.
The Rudras have been proclaimed by you as abiding in forms of five different colors;
O Amṛtākha, Ruru, Candra, salutations to you, O Jñānabhairavī!
O you with fangs bared and a tongue like lightning, with eyes like palm-leaf bolts and a terrifying face;
I bow to you, O Goddess of the lords of gods, Aghorā, possessed of terrible prowess.
Homage to you, Jvālāmukhī, Vegavatī, and Umādevī;
to the Yoginī Śrayādevī, Gaurī, Lakṣmī, and Sarasvatī.
The goddess Haṃsasvarādhakā is Gomuhī, the slayer of Śakti.
Kroṣṭakī, Śubhagādevī, Durgā, and likewise Kātyāyanī.
The one known as Nityaklinnā is red and supreme, consisting of a single syllable;
likewise Brāhmī, Māheśvarī, Kaumārī, and Vaiṣṇavī.
You are Vārāhī, Māhendrī, and Cāmuṇḍā with a terrifying countenance;
you are indeed Yogeśī, O Goddess of gods, adorned by the eight families (kulāṣṭaka).
O Goddess who upholds the eight groups of eight, you are Lakṣmī of manifold forms;
you are indeed Aindrī in the east, Āgneyī in the southeast, Yāmyā in the south, and Nairṛtyavāhinī in the southwest.
The Vāyavyā, Kauverī, and Īśānī have been proclaimed; likewise Prayāga, Varuṇā, Kolā, Aṭṭahāsa, and Jayantikā.
In the Caritra [region], Kāmraka, and likewise Devīkoṭa in due order;
as well as Kālī, Umādevī, and Devadūtī—homage be to you!
O Bhadrakālī, O Mahāmāyā, O Carmmamuṇḍā, O terrifying one!
O you who are both great and subtle, O Great Peaceful One; salutations to you, whose form is Śakti.
"O Bhūḥ Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! At the end of the *svāhā* [mantra], O Kṣamā, show compassion!
O Mahāmāyā, I desire knowledge; I wish to know this."
The man who recites this hymn at the three junctions of the day attains his desired wishes and becomes beloved by women.
[Thus ends the hymn to Mahāmāyā on the state of the essential identity of Śiva and Śakti.]

The tawny-eyed one with red hair, uttering "kiṇi kiṇi," adorned with a garland of tinkling bells, with fangs and a mouth, possessing a wrathful nature that removes all fear, holding a vessel in her hand and making a roar— a clearly manifest lion’s roar, "lalalalalavalam"— the varvara sound, the reality of the sky.
I bow to the Kṣetrapāla, who is invoked for the sake of spirits, ghosts, and others, and who is measured by the house.
Clad in red garments, with a mass of flaming tawny matted locks, and possessing a garland of flames,
the son of Gaurī, Vaṭukanātha— resplendent like the rising sun and fair-complexioned from contact with the golden hue of his mother Gaurī— I bow down to that fierce one.
O destroyer of the suffering that flows from the senses, who has pacified the fear of existence, you who bring an end to all obstacles!
Gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaiṃ! O you whose horn is the sky, whose movement traverses the firmament, you who are the essence of all accomplishments and all aims!
Oṃ hrūṃ! O you who move with the speed of the wind and the elephant-goad mudrā, you who abide in the many forms of the rat!
Oṃ hrīṃ hraṃ hāṃ gāṃ! O Gaṇeśa, you who possess the elephant and the two birds, O Lord of Obstacles, homage to you!
She is Icchā, Jñānā, and Kriyā; she is the consort of the Asuras, she is Sāśrayā, and she is named Maṅgalā.
She is Gaurī, she is Durgā, the auspicious Bhagavatī, Mātṛkā, and Carmamuṇḍā. She is Brahmā and Viṣṇu, she is the totality of the host of planets, Bhairavī, and the Kṣetrapālas.
I bow to you, the Yoginī, who possesses manifold forms and various heavy wings.

The letter *ū* has eternal feet, the arms *ha*, *sa*, *kṣa*, *ma*, and *ra*, it bears fire as its emblem, and its body is the tiger-skin of the wind; its head is the full moon with a dot (*bindu*) and a nasal resonance (*nāda*), joined with the upward-pointing [flame].

May the Lord Bhairava—who is the form of mantra, whose rain-clouds are the cessation of all signs, and who is the straight, supreme art—protect us; or rather, may the venerable Kujeśa, the preeminent teacher of all, protect us.
Brahmāṇī has a face as gentle as a lotus or the moon; Māheśvarī possesses playful grace; Kaumārī is the destroyer of the pride of enemies; Vaiṣṇavī holds a discus as her weapon;
Vārāhī has a snout as terrible and rumbling as a thundercloud; and Aindrī wields the thunderbolt as her weapon.
May Cāmuṇḍā, Gaṇanātha, Bhairava, and the hosts of Mothers protect me.
Dark-red in complexion, with three eyes, her breasts heavy with weight, she moves with the gait of an intoxicated elephant;
her lips are like the *bimba* fruit, her eyes are wide and wandering, her hips are broad and fleshy, and she is adorned with the splendor of jewels.

May she known as the illustrious Kubjikā, who dwells upon the limbs of the gods, who is radiant with the beauty of excellent flowers, whose mass of hair is dark and curly, and who is tranquil, swiftly bestow the abundant and unfailing flood of divine knowledge.

Mārkaṇḍeya took birth through your grace for the sake of bestowing favor; he whose power was such that the Daityas, though equal to Brahmā, were crushed by him, and who brought joy to the gods with his hymns of praise while still in the womb.
Therefore, let him be born of the goddess Caṇḍikā for your glory.
Seated upon the pericarp of a full-blown lotus is the supreme Śrī Siddhilakṣmī,
white as camphor, crystal, the moon, and the kunda flower; she is the remover of all sins and the one who always renders the manifold sufferings of saṃsāra motionless within the lotus-hand of Hari.
May she who possesses glorious five lotus-faces, ten arms, and stands upon a corpse protect you.
Nirvāṇa, free from conceptual construction, the cause of the ultimate cessation, changeless, the syllable KṢA, the time of HŪṂ, the Vajra-beholder, whose vehicle is the bearer of oblations (fire),
the fierce one, the state of madness, the sound PHET, the roar of fire, the all-pervading Bhṛgu, the Terrifier, the wielder of the trident.
The skull-topped staff, the celestial sword together with the hand-drum, Bhairava, and Kṣetrapāla.
In the east, south, west, and north are the auspicious ones; in the east and other directions stand Vāmā and the others.
In the field are Kṣetreśa, Vaṭu, Bhūta, Durgā, Haragaṇa, and Herambanātha.
In the cremation ground is the primordial god Svara, two-armed, who removes defects such as fear and the like.
This is the ritual procedure for the lamp offering, which consists of eternal bliss and is ever-joyful.
Just as armor serves as a protection against the blows of weapons,
even so may peace serve as a protection against the blows of fate.

May the Kṣetrapālas of their respective abodes, together with Brahmāṇī and the others, along with Aśitāṅga Mahābhairava, Gaṇa, Vaṭuka, Yoginīs, and Kṣetrapālas, together with their limbs, hosts, and retinues, and the world-protectors such as Indra in the cardinal and intermediate directions, be well-pleased and granters of strength.

May there be long life, health, sovereignty, progeny, wealth, fortune, and the increase of lineage for the patron, along with his attendants and retinue; and may they become bestowers of boons according to the fruit of this hymn of praise.
There is no other refuge; you alone are my refuge.
Therefore, O Supreme Goddess, protect me, protect me with your compassionate nature!
The sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*);
the shadow of the covenant (*samaya-cchāyā*); the libation (*tarpaṇa*); the gratification of the departed spirits (*pretas*) and so forth; the offering of the mandala.
O Mother, whose single form is manifold; O Pūrṇeśvarī in the east, Bhūteśī in the north-east, Gaganopamā in the south-west, and Niḥśeṣeśvarī in the south;
O Jñānāgamya in the west, Kujeśvarī among the hosts of Kula, and Gāyakā in the western direction.
I bow to the auspicious Vāmā, the mother of the universe, the sovereign of vision, and the perfection of all accomplishments.
Nosiya || Oṃ hrāṃ, svāhā to the reality of the self (ātmatattva).

Having sipped water according to the three principles: *hrāṃ* to the principle of the self (*ātmatattva*), *svāhā*; *hrāṃ* to the principle of knowledge (*vidyātattva*), *svāhā*; *hrūṃ* to the principle of Śiva (*śivatattva*), *svāhā*.
Homage to the Guru.

the Guru is indeed the entire universe—to that illustrious Guru, salutations.

The sentence.

Above that is Kāla joined with the final letter of the alphabet, and above that is the supreme seed-syllable of Fire, a thousandfold, ending with the moon-drop and the point (*laya*). It is like the petal of a white lotus, flowing with a stream of milk.
A wicked wife constantly burns the family; indeed, her sin is as great as Mount Meru.
Dudu.
By the command of Śiva, I constantly bathe Kāmadhenu and Śrava, who have filled the earth with a stream of milk like nectar.
Hour by hour.
[This is] curd for the god Umāpati, who is most beloved by the gods;
by which bath the station called Vācchāpaṭala is obtained.
Ghera.
O you who are filled with clarified butter, O you who are filled with the Liṅga, O wielder of the Pināka bow!
In the form of the power of fire, O Śiva, protect the worlds from distress.
Who is this?
Gomukhī is the forest of the elements, the supreme favorite of the gods;
it is the bath that is obtained by means of which one gains the wish-fulfilling tree of desires.
Sākhara.
O God, this sugar-candy is always cool and highly palatable to the mind;
it has been bathed with moonlight and bestows unbroken strength.
The five nectars.
Likewise, I bathe [the deity] with the five products of the cow and other substances, which are infused with the five Brahmans and joined with the five materials, using the five tips.
Bathing the eyebrows.

The attendant.
May this divine sandalwood paste, enchanting with its fragrance and other qualities,
which adorns the forehead, be accepted.
Anointed with sandalwood paste brings merit, purity, and the destruction of sin;
it constantly wards off calamities and bestows prosperity, sovereignty, and happiness.
Sindūra.
Vīreśvarī, the Great Heroine, adorned with the ashes of heroes;
the Goddess who attracts the three worlds, most excellent and crimson as vermilion.
Unbroken.
O Goddess, grant me my desired boon— unbroken and inexhaustible desire that bestows the attainment of Dharma, Kāma, and Artha— and in the hereafter, the supreme goal.
View.
It is gracefully present within those of vast vision through meditation and heroic eyes;
it is the stainless world of the moon, sun, and fire, manifesting through the eye of equanimity.
The sacrificers.
The sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*) is the supreme purifier; O Prajāpati, it was born together with you in the beginning.
Granting long life, fragrant, and exceedingly bright, this sacred thread is the highest splendor.
